REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - JANUARY 12, 2026 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at cerritos.gov and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.gov or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
Order of Agenda
The City Council, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at cerritos.gov, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 6.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.gov or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk at 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703 no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting and retained with the official meeting record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact City of Cerritos ADA/504 Coordinator, Drew Schneider, at (562) 916-1314 at least 72 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to public meetings.

This section is reserved for public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and items not listed on the agenda but that are within the subject matter jurisdiction of the legislative body. Verbal comments may be limited to three minutes per speaker, subject to the Mayor/Chair extending to a maximum of five minutes per speaker, with a total time allotted not to exceed 45 minutes unless the Mayor/Chair extends.

Items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion. During this part of the meeting the City Manager/Executive Director or designated staff will have an opportunity to report on various City matters and/or respond verbally to questions or comments from the prior City Council meeting, including any request by the City Council to provide a brief supplemental report or brief follow-up response to items from the prior City Council meeting's agenda.
11B.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition,
verbal reports will also be provided in such cases where the City Council-appointed delegate and/or alternate is unable to attend a scheduled meeting, and there is insufficient time to schedule an agenda item for Council consideration of another alternate, necessitating a Mayor's urgency appointment. Requests may also be made of staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item, except to cancel or reschedule a City Council public meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD MONDAY,
JANUARY 12, 2026, 7:00 PM, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL,
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Chaplain Joseph Torres, Calvary Chapel Artesia.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Carver Academy Student Council.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jennifer Hong
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Council/Agency Member Sophia M. Tse
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Lynda P. Johnson
  Mayor/Chair Frank Aurelio Yokoyama

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  A proclamation was made by the City Council honoring:

  Rogan Girard (City Employee Retirement).

5B.  Informational report providing a status update on water and sewer infrastructure,
  including an emergency repair of the C-4 well and purchase of imported water
  (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Alvin Papa, Director of Public Works/City Engineer. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Case van der Linden expressed concern regarding the City’s water and sewer
  infrastructure, regular maintenance schedules, and methods of reporting.

  Steve Stallings in opposition to proposed water and sewer rate adjustments as
  presented in the City’s Notice of Public Hearing on Proposed Water and Sewer Rate
  Adjustment.
 City of Cerritos  Monday, January 12, 2026, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 2 of 15

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5B.  (continued)

  Kurtis Forsythe expressed concern regarding his recent interactions and meetings
  with City officials and Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department personnel, related to
  the City’s proposed water and sewer rate adjustments. He also submitted documents
  for the official record. (Documents submitted to the City Council at a public meeting
  are considered public record. Public requests for copies of the full-text redacted
  written correspondence can be made during regular business hours to the Office of
  the City Clerk.)

  Benjamin Ao spoke in support of the proposed water and sewer rate adjustments as
  presented in the City’s Notice of Public Hearing on Proposed Water and Sewer Rate
  Adjustment but requested alternate considerations with regard to the schedule and
  amount of increase.

  Karen Wilson expressed concern regarding potential mail tampering and placement
  of protest forms by private individuals into private mailboxes.

  The following individuals spoke in opposition to proposed water and sewer rate
  adjustments as presented in the City’s Notice of Public Hearing on Proposed Water
  and Sewer Rate Adjustment:

  Robert Shavelle
  Charlie Joslin
  Daisy Lagasca

  The following individuals spoke in support of proposed water and sewer rate
  adjustments as presented in the City’s Notice of Public Hearing on Proposed Water
  and Sewer Rate Adjustment:

  Eder Rabanales
  Al Barlevy
  Catherine Pascual
  Deborah Berry

  Cynthia Nava, City Clerk, announced that prior to the meeting, the City Council
  received full-text, unredacted copies of the four (4) written comments submitted for
  Item 5B, by the deadline listed on the agenda and for inclusion in the official record.
  Requests for copies of the written comments submitted for this meeting can be made
  during regular business hours to the Office of the City Clerk.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  There was no action taken on this item.

(minutes continue on the next page)
 City of Cerritos  Monday, January 12, 2026, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 3 of 15

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period for items not listed on the meeting
  agenda but that were within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the
  Consent Calendar, and Closed Session.

  Daisy Lagasca inquired regarding community organizations listed on the 2026
  Community Calendar and expressed concern regarding potential public health
  issues related to water contaminants.

  Tamara Glasser expressed concern her personal personnel issues as a City
  employee.

  Case van der Linden expressed concern regarding potential radiation emission
  from the Southern California Edison Bovine Substation and inquired regarding
  inspection and maintenance of fire hydrants located within the City.

  Mel Cortez expressed concern regarding public safety in the City and inquired
  regarding location of automated license plate readers. He also submitted
  documents for the official record. (Documents submitted to the City Council at a
  public meeting are considered public record. Public requests for copies of the full-
  text redacted written correspondence can be made during regular business hours
  to the Office of the City Clerk.)

  Charlie Joslin expressed concern regarding the proposed low-income assistance
  program related and proposed water and sewer rate adjustments. He also inquired
  regarding public comments emailed to the City Council and spoke regarding the
  Cerritos-on-Wheels and Dial-A-Ride program.

  Shawn Quarles expressed concern regarding surveillance cameras installed by
  private individuals on public property and other areas in Cerritos neighborhoods.

  Deborah Berry expressed concern regarding the length and conduct of City
  Council meetings.

  Samar Malouf expressed concern regarding traffic control in her neighborhood
  and requested placement of speed humps to deter vehicles driving at excessive
  speeds.

  The Mayor announced that prior to the meeting, the City Council/Successor Agency
  members received full-text, unredacted copies of the six (6) written comments
  submitted for Item 6, inclusive of two (2) comments for Item 7C, one (1) comment
  for Item 7I, and one (1) comment for Item 7J, by the deadline listed on the agenda
  and for inclusion in the official record. Requests for copies of the written comments
  submitted for this meeting can be made during regular business hours to the Office
  of the City Clerk.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.
